title: Rebuilding Trust With My Cousin After the Inheritance Dispute
script: Narrator: [honestly] When our grandfather passed away, my cousin Reza and I ended up on opposite sides of a disagreement about how his small house should be divided.
Narrator: [reflective] Neither of us was purely greedy, I think, but grief has a way of making people defend positions more fiercely than the situation actually requires.
Narrator: [honestly] I accused him of pressuring our grandfather before he died, and even though I had no real proof, the words caused damage that lasted for two years.
Narrator: [thoughtful] We avoided family gatherings where the other might appear, and if someone mentioned his name, I would simply change the subject rather than respond honestly.
Narrator: [reflective] Despite the silence, I noticed something uncomfortable: I missed him far more than I missed being right about the house.
Narrator: [honestly] Last year, his daughter got married, and I had to decide whether pride mattered more than showing up for a cousin I had known since childhood.
Narrator: [determined] I went to the wedding, and even though the conversation between us felt stiff at first, we ended up talking quietly near the food table for almost an hour.
Narrator: [honestly] I told him I regretted the accusation, and that even if I still disagreed about the house, I shouldn't have questioned his character so publicly.
Narrator: [relieved] To my surprise, he admitted he had also said things he regretted, and that the silence between us had bothered him more than he'd ever let on.
Narrator: [thoughtful] We still haven't fully resolved the property question, and honestly, we may never agree on it completely.
Narrator: [peacefully] However, we agreed that the house wasn't worth losing each other over, especially since our grandfather would have hated seeing us this divided.
Narrator: [warmly] Now we speak every few weeks, and although the topic of the house still occasionally comes up, it no longer controls the entire relationship.
Narrator: [with a small smile] If I've learned anything, it's that being technically right rarely feels as good as people expect, especially once the people around you start disappearing.
